archetype.name: Play-In Team (paint-and-foul-line offense)
archetype.definition: A roughly break-even team by margin, a clear step up from two bottom-tier seasons, that scores by living at the rim and the line through an elite frontcourt but gives back too much in the paint and at the point of attack to climb higher yet.

report.headline: A .500 team in a 4-6 shirt, carried by Zion and the foul line
report.take:
New Orleans is 4-6, last in a Southwest where everyone else is above .500, and sits 18th on the site. The record undersells it a little. The Pelicans have been outscored by just 3 points over ten games, a margin worth 5 wins rather than 4, and a Net Rtg of -0.3 is essentially an average team. For a franchise coming off 21-61 and 26-56, average is real progress. Last year's Net Rtg was -4.5, and the DRtg has improved from 118.9 to 115.6.

The engine is the frontcourt, graded A+. Zion Williamson is 6th on the PF tab with a 68.8 TS % and a team-best 1.4 Win Shares, and the offense has been built around him. The Pelicans take the league's smallest share of shots from three, a 3PA Rate of 32 against a league average of 43, and they make up for it by getting to the line at the 3rd-highest FT Rate. That combination yields the 6th-best TS % even though their 3P % ranks 24th. Karlo Matković has added spacing in his minutes: 16 threes on a 76.2 TS % and a +14.7 On-Off.

The flaws sit on the perimeter and in the paint. The backcourt (B-) and wings (C-) score far less efficiently than the bigs. Jeremiah Fears and Dejounte Murray are both in the low 50s in TS %, with On-Offs around -7 to -8. Defensively, opponents get to the rim often and finish there at the 26th-worst rate. Opposing point guards have averaged 31.9 points, ranked 30th against their own norms. The 115.6 DRtg also looks a bit flattering, because opponents are shooting just 32.3% from three, 6th-lowest in the league. That figure is more likely to rise than to hold.

The ten games have swung hard. A four-game losing streak, including an overtime loss at Denver and two one- or three-point losses, gave way to a four-game winning streak, two of those wins also in overtime. Then came losses to Minnesota and at the Clippers. Close games have roughly evened out. What remains is a team scoring 120.5 a game (2nd) while allowing 120.8 (26th), and that profile points toward the play-in range if Zion stays on the floor.

strengths.title: Zion-led frontcourt overwhelms inside
strengths.body: Williamson's 68.8 TS % at a 21.8 USG % is the most efficient high-volume scoring on the roster, and the frontcourt grades A+. He is the only rotation regular with both a strong BPM and a positive On-Off. Queen and Matković support him, and the group's sustainability hinges mostly on his health. Yves Missi, listed Out, thins the depth behind Queen at center.

strengths.title: Free throws power elite efficiency
strengths.body: New Orleans ranks 3rd in FT Rate, well above the league average and far above last season's 28.4. That is the main reason a team shooting poorly from three still posts the 6th-best TS %. A foul-drawing profile built on a dominant interior scorer tends to hold up better than hot shooting does.

strengths.title: Margin better than the record
strengths.body: Ten games yield a -3 point differential, worth 5 wins rather than 4, and the last five went 3-2 with a +1.6 per-game margin. The ORtg of 115.3 ranks 13th, comfortably above the league's 113.4. That is the base of a team that can win as often as it loses.

concerns.title: Paint defense is leaking badly
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 70.7% at the rim, 26th in the league and well above the 65.2 average, and they get there at the 23rd-highest rate. The rim-rate problem is not new, since last season's Opp Rim Rate was 33.0. The finishing allowed is worse this year, which suggests a structural issue rather than noise.

concerns.title: Point guards are feasting
concerns.body: Opposing PGs average 31.9 points and 9.7 assists. Against what those players do elsewhere, the scoring allowed ranks dead last. Opposing power forwards are also scoring well above their norms. With Memphis's A backcourt and Golden State's A- backcourt on deck, this is the matchup most likely to sink games.

concerns.title: Opponent threes likely to regress
concerns.body: Opponents are hitting just 32.3% from deep, 6th-lowest, while the same defense ranks poorly at the rim. Three-point defense swings a lot over ten games. If that number drifts toward the league's 34.8, the 115.6 DRtg gets worse before it gets better.

trend.note: The season so far has been an 0-4 start, a four-game winning streak and two straight losses. The last five run slightly better than the season overall, but overtime and one-possession games have decided most of the swings.

weekAhead.headline: Four home games, but Golden State twice plus Memphis and Denver
weekAhead.body:
Four of the five games are at home, but only Brooklyn (2-8, 28th in ORtg) is a soft draw. Golden State is 7-3 and 7th on the site, with the league's best 3P % and the 2nd-best TS %. Memphis is 6-3 with the 8th-best defense, and Denver already beat New Orleans twice in October. A low-volume three-point team facing Golden State's shooting twice is the matchup of the week.

The path is through the paint. Golden State keeps opponents away from the rim better than anyone (Opp Rim Rate 1st), but when teams get there it allows the 29th-worst finishing, and its frontcourt grades D-. Denver also allows a high rim rate. Memphis is the stingier inside defense and the best rebounding team in the league. Two wins is the realistic middle; three would be a statement.

keyMatchups.title: Zion against soft rim protection
keyMatchups.body: Golden State (71.2 Opp Rim FG %) and Denver (68.4) both rank in the bottom third at defending the rim, and Golden State's frontcourt grades D-. These are the games where Williamson's volume at the rim and the line should translate. Golden State's league-best Opp Rim Rate means the shots will have to be earned.

keyMatchups.title: Warriors shooting versus thin perimeter
keyMatchups.body: Golden State shoots 39.5% from three, 1st in the league, and takes far more of its shots from deep than New Orleans does. If the Pelicans' unusually low opponent 3P % is going to correct, two games against this offense are where it happens. That would wipe out much of the free-throw edge.

keyMatchups.title: Memphis guards and the glass
keyMatchups.body: Memphis brings an A backcourt against a defense that has allowed the most scoring over expectation to point guards. The Grizzlies also lead the league in rebounds per game. New Orleans's 24th-ranked ORB % means few second chances in that one.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the opponent 3P % holds up through two Golden State games, the clearest test of how real the improved defense is.

restOfSeason.body:
The margin says this is a near-.500 team, and the parts that drive it are mostly durable: a top-tier interior scorer, a foul-line habit, and a frontcourt that outclasses most. Against that, the perimeter defense and rim finishing allowed look structural, and the low opponent three-point shooting should drift back toward the league. That likely nudges the DRtg up. Close-game luck is roughly neutral, so there is no big correction coming in either direction.

From 4-6 with 72 games left, a final record in the mid-to-high 30s in wins is the honest expectation, with something like 34 to 40 wins, enough to chase a play-in spot. Health in the frontcourt and any improvement from Fears and Murray in efficiency move the range most. A real jump would need the guards to stop bleeding points at the point of attack.
swingFactors: Backcourt efficiency from Fears and Murray

confidence.note: Ten games, three of them in overtime and several decided by one or two possessions.
